title: Enabling the Systemic Delivery of Oncolytic HAdVs by Cationic Peptide Coating
content: Advanced metastatic prostate cancer is incurable due to genetic instability and heterogeneity, leading to rapid acquisition of resistance to all standard treatments. Oncolytic Adenoviruses have been extensively evaluated as therapeutics capable of overcoming the shortfalls of the current standard of care. However, factors such as poor uptake in prostate cancer cells, binding to erythrocytes and circulating blood factors, and clearance by hepatic Kupffer cells have prevented efficient systemic delivery and targeting of metastatic tumours by adenoviruses. In this work, we aimed to improve systemic delivery by coating the highly potent and selective Ad-3Δ-A20T mutant with cationic peptides. We hypothesised that these agents would protect the viral particle from detrimental blood factors and improve transduction and efficacy by increasing the dose at the sites of distant tumour lesions. Initial proof-of-concept studies with the cationic amino acids lysine and arginine successfully enhanced attachment, infection, and consequent cytotoxicity of Ad-3Δ-A20T in prostate cancer cell lines. Similar promising results were observed with the cationic peptide K2A5 in preliminary in vitro studies. Additional cationic lysine- and arginine-containing peptides were designed and evaluated. In vivo studies, utilising a combination of both live imaging and ex vivo techniques, demonstrated that K2A5 and the cationic peptide KRGD decreased adenoviral transduction to the liver at early time points after intravenous administration. KRGD also improved tumour uptake in a time-dependent manner. In summary, our research highlights that cationic peptides can coat and neutralise the negatively charged adenoviral particle, thereby increasing tumour bioavailability while subverting rapid systemic clearance.
